messages.content: What kind of fertilizer is best for growing tomatoes?

function.name: soil_analysis_analyze_soil_type
function.description: Analyze a type of soil and provides characteristics about it. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

soil_type.description: The type of the soil. For example, loam, sandy, etc.

parameters_needed.description: Optional specific characteristics of the soil to analyze.

message.content: For tomatoes, a balanced fertilizer with a higher middle number (N-P-K) is usually best—something like 10-10-10 or 5-10-5. Tomatoes benefit from a bit more phosphorus (the middle number) to promote strong root development and fruit set, and a moderate amount of potassium (the last number) for overall plant health and disease resistance. A common recommendation is a 5-10-5 or 10-10-10 applied at planting and then again when the first fruits appear. Organic options such as composted manure or fish emulsion also work well, especially if you prefer natural amendments.
